sharedSkillEdits.edits: `SKILL.md` states that a prompt or brief naming the skill is its invocation.
It adds a Reads section, which lists the repository files the skill reads and what it does when each is missing.

code-review.edits: It also drops the route to `setup-matt-pocock-skills` when the tracker configuration is missing, and its spec search reviews against the issue's implementation contract where the tracker configuration says which comment or body holds it. It pins both comparison commits and the merge-base, runs the bundled ownership-facts.mjs collector before the independent axes, and passes its facts and codebase-design's Ownership check to Standards. Both prompts apply that section's cleanup allowance against the PR body and retain contract-based judgment and the contribution guide's Findings route. Spec discovery follows the validator’s selected source/revision and prepared/body-mode rules, including only the exact unchanged inventoried legacy exception; later comments cannot replace a migrated body contract.

codebase-design.edits: It adds the shared Ownership check section: value owners, triggers and cost read, wrapping and extraction defaults, deferred seams, narrow touched-code cleanup, contract disagreement routing, and capability/policy and vendored UI examples. Its description and Reads section expose that reference.

domain-modeling.edits: It also has glossary and ADR edits made on a branch of their own in a checkout the session owns, never in a shared checkout on the default branch, and delivered as the repository's contribution guide directs. It creates `docs/adr/` with its index where the repo indexes its documentation directories, and `ADR-FORMAT.md` adds each new ADR to that index, and keeps a superseded ADR, marking it superseded with a link to the ADR that supersedes it.

grill-with-docs.edits: It composes grilling and domain-modeling with to-spec then to-tickets, publishing one cross-repository specification and proposed direct tickets for independent exact-revision review. It reuses dated decisions, applies the contribution guide’s inference boundary, reports native-link failures, and handles amendment grills through specification revisions and delta tickets, with Reads fallbacks. It invokes codebase-design and applies its single Ownership check to proposed designs during the interview.

grilling.edits: It also asks the frontier in rounds and keeps each round short, asking the frontier questions that unblock the most first when the frontier holds more than the user can weigh at once. It reuses recorded dated answers, limits owner questions to one-way doors and unchosen values under the full inference test, lists qualifying inferences for owner veto and retains grill-answer and plan-approval gates without an extra quiz. A composite skill continues to publication after the interview; its Reads section supplies the contribution-guide fallback.

implement.edits: `SKILL.md` drops `disable-model-invocation` and `agents/openai.yaml` enables `policy.allow_implicit_invocation`. It reads branch and validation requirements from the contribution guide instead of repeating its branch rule. It replaces self-review and direct delivery with validated draft pull request creation using `pr`, then stops for a separate `review` agent. Given review findings, it pushes fixes to the same draft pull request and stops again. A factory without a configured review run retains delivery through `babysit` under its installed rules, including applicable internal reviews, merge conditions and worker handoffs. Both delivery routes cite the contribution guide's Worker handoff condition before reporting success and carry its head, trusted required-check authority, check-location, command and outcome record. Without a contribution guide, it uses a dedicated branch and available checks before opening the draft. It applies codebase-design’s single Ownership check to its change, including that section’s contract-disagreement route, with a missing-skill fallback in Reads.

improve-codebase-architecture.edits: It also makes the grilling loop's domain-model edits on the branch and checkout `domain-modeling` directs. Named ownership exploration uses codebase-design's Ownership check for misplaced values, configuration kinds and surprising layout, passing that reference to its exploring sub-agent.

pr.edits: Evidence requires screenshots on an orphan `pr-assets/<topic>` branch and image links by full commit SHA, and refers to the installed GitHub repository configuration rules for permanent asset-branch retention during cleanup, preserving the branch when those rules are missing. Its template ends with a Related issue section after Merge Danger, holding a closing or partial-work reference or a Direct change reason, and keeps the four sections in order with any other material in a subsection of the section it belongs to. Evidence lists every check run on the final commit with its outcome and explains any required check not run, and Merge Danger names the change's relevant limits and a breaking change's impact and migration. Summary condenses the visual examples while retaining every visual type and its selection, context, placement and copyable-target guidance. This file keeps upstream's credits below unchanged. The `show-me` material those credits name is covered by HumanLayer's MIT License, whose notice follows Matt Pocock's at the end of this file; adoption also installs it beside the skills.

research.edits: Its description covers assigned artifacts and delegated triage research. The current run performs the investigation directly, including when delegated, instead of starting another background researcher. It publishes an assigned artifact at its destination with source citations; an issue artifact needs no repository findings file or index edit. Without an assigned artifact, it defaults to a single Markdown findings file where the repository's documentation rules or convention put such notes, such as beside the usage or development topic they serve, and adds it to that directory's index, creating it when those rules require one. It retains the missing-rules placement fallback. An issue or pull request artifact is posted as the installed comment rules' section it names says.

to-spec.edits: It also drops the route to `setup-matt-pocock-skills` when the tracker configuration is missing, and publishes the spec awaiting an independent readiness review, after any revision notice and with the labels the repository's rules require, instead of applying `ready-for-agent` itself; a spec broken into tickets gets its readiness after they are published. Each step that publishes an issue body or posts a comment on a hosted tracker names the installed comment rules' section to read first. It replaces test-seam re-confirmation with dated decision reuse and evidence for independent review, routes only unresolved owner choices, and publishes one direct issue-body specification in the repository containing most work. It copies decision dates and quoted words, returns the published or amended specification to its caller for ticket sequencing, and handles amendments with fresh revision review and readiness.

to-tickets.edits: It also drops both routes to `setup-matt-pocock-skills`. Expand–contract batches that cannot each stay green become one ticket instead of sharing an integration branch, since every ticket merges on its own with its checks passing. On a real tracker, parent and blocker links are native only, and a link that cannot be created is reported instead of written into the body. Tickets are published awaiting an independent readiness review instead of carrying `ready-for-agent`, and the local ticket template's status is `state:triage`. Work that must be shown on a live system splits into a source ticket and a live-acceptance ticket that no merge closes, and nobody edits a ready ticket to record progress. Each step that publishes an issue body or posts a comment on a hosted tracker names the installed comment rules' section to read first. It replaces the owner breakdown quiz with evidence for independent split review and the orchestrating agent’s final split authority. Grill publication uses one specification parent across responsible repositories, copies dated decisions and quoted words, reports exact native-link failures, applies the full inference boundary and handles authorized delta amendments with renewed exact-revision readiness.

triage.edits: `OUT-OF-SCOPE.md` and `agents/openai.yaml` are unchanged from it. `SKILL.md` keeps upstream's invocation, discovery buckets, outcomes, and templates, and names its roles by Repo Canon's label families: `type:` categories and five `state:` roles naming whom an issue waits on, with `wontfix` as the closing outcome. Upstream's `needs-info` becomes `state:reporter`, kept for a fact only an outside reporter holds, beside `state:grill` and `state:owner` for the owner's intent and answers; `ready-for-human` becomes `state:owner`, which is not readiness; and triage sets a `priority:` label by the installed rules' rubric without replacing a person's. It replaces the single triage procedure with routing by uncertainty: research and independent acceptance for code-bound requests, and for intent-bound ones fact-finding, inference the orchestrating agent can cite, and a grilling session with the owner that publishes direct specification/ticket contracts for independent review. It routes every question through the orchestrating agent, with its decision inbox as the one channel to the owner. It also points the label mapping and meanings at the installed triage label configuration instead of the setup skill, replaces the disclaimer with the installed comment rules' section that each posting step names, adds who does what, notes that a quick state override is the maintainer's own review applied through the readiness command, and has acceptance choose between `state:ready`, `state:ready` with the factory's skip label, and `state:owner`. The Reads section also covers `ready.mjs` and the installed comment rules. `AGENT-BRIEF.md` keeps upstream's principles, template, and examples, and adds the decisions, progress and live-acceptance principles and the triage notes. Its reference condenses durability and behavioral guidance, repeated template placeholders, and bug, enhancement, PR and negative examples while retaining the original seven fields, every example contract, available-input and decision provenance, independent acceptance, owner-review designation and revision/readiness semantics. `ready.mjs` is Repo Canon's original readiness acceptance command. The acceptance step calls it to apply the reviewed revision and confirm the validator recorded it. The research handoff identifies the issue comments as the assigned research artifacts and destinations, composing with the research skill's direct investigation and assigned publication method. The code-bound brief followed by triage notes and intent-bound fact-finding notes remain distinct deliverables. A second mode runs the skill unattended as the factory's triage run: it researches, writes and reviews the brief itself, cites only repository records for inferred intent, writes nothing on the tracker, and ends with a run result that asks the factory to post the brief or question and apply its labels. The skill points to the contribution guide and installed rules for the triage policy instead of restating it. Its method consolidates mode and role summaries, folds resumption into context gathering, and states the reporter template and Reads fallbacks compactly while preserving the research, independent acceptance, readiness and factory-result procedures. It distinguishes prepared comment publication from explicit body-mode publication, preserves one verbatim Original request and the unchanged inventoried legacy exception, keeps host attestation separate from mutable reports, and checks v2 platform-observation freshness through the validator. The template, examples and independent review add Seams after Out of scope, citing codebase-design’s single Ownership check definition. The writer records its result and independent review assesses honesty, Value owner, consumers, reversibility and cost, while the validator checks structure. The readiness command also checks body-observation freshness for v3 Seams exemption results. Its intent-bound grill publishes one specification and proposed direct tickets through to-spec/to-tickets, instead of draft Agent Briefs for the orchestrator to file. Independent acceptance checks the split and seam/factual evidence without an owner quiz, preserves original intake publication rules and applies direct-contract shapes without redundant briefs or category labels. It handles amendment revisions and exact native-link failures.

wayfinder.edits: It also drops the route to `setup-matt-pocock-skills` when the tracker configuration is missing, counts only native child and blocking links on a tracker that has them, reporting a link that cannot be created, and fills every map section but Decisions so far, including Out of scope, with words rather than only its template comment. Each step that publishes an issue body or posts a comment on a hosted tracker names the installed comment rules' section to read first.

writing-for-agents.edits: Its pruning reference keeps requirements in the rules or contribution guide that hold them, with skills stating the method, and puts repository-specific agent constraints in the file a repository names for them where it installs `AGENTS.md` as shared content.

docs/agents/issue-tracker.md.edits: Creating an issue writes the body in the matching issue form's sections and passes it as a body file. Reading an issue names the latest Agent Brief comment as its implementation contract. Readiness labels are applied only through the triage skill's readiness command. Wayfinding child and blocking links are native only: the task list, `Part of` and `Blocked by` body fallbacks are removed, an uncreatable link is reported, and the frontier query reads native sub-issues and dependencies.

docs/agents/triage-labels.md.edits: The roles map to Repo Canon's `state:` labels, which the GitHub rules hold; the Meaning column becomes a Waits on column, and a grill state has no upstream role. A paragraph says that readiness is a review of the current contract revision applied through the triage skill's readiness command after the revision notice, and that an issue left with no state gets `state:triage`. The closing line inviting edits is removed, since adoption keeps the file.
